'''''Nematanthus''''' is a genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Gesneriaceae]].  All of its [[species]] are [[endemic]] to [[Brazil]].<ref name=POWO_331798-2/> Compared to other gesneriads, ''Nematanthus'' has [[leaf|leaves]] that are small, [[Succulent plant|succulent]], and hard-surfaced.  The plant has a trailing, branching, and spreading habit; it is generally an [[epiphyte]] in nature and a hanging-basket plant in cultivation. The [[flower]] has fused [[petal]]s. In some species, the flower has a "pouch" at the bottom. The fancied resemblance of such flowers to a [[goldfish]] gives these plants the common name '''goldfish plant''' or '''guppy plant'''.

Hummingbirds will often feed from the nectar-filled "goldfish" flowers.

==Description==
''Nematanthus'' species are [[Perennial plant|perennials]] or subshrubs, typically growing [[Epiphyte|epiphytically]], less often in [[humus]]-filled pockets on rocks. Their leaves are often reddish underneath. Their flowers have fused [[petal]]s and vary quite widely in shape. Some have flowers with a "pouch" on the lower surface of the flower and a small opening (particularly those commonly cultivated). Others have flowers that are twisted through 180° when fully open ([[Resupination|resupinate]]), so that if pouched, the pouch is at the top. Resupinate flowers may be brightly coloured, funnel-shaped and compressed from side to side, or white and bell-shaped. Some species have flowers that are borne on long [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]] and hang down below the plant, others have short pedicels so that the flowers are close to the stem.<ref name=ChauPerr17/><ref name=GS/>

==Taxonomy==
The genus ''Nematanthus'' was first described by [[Heinrich Schrader (botanist)|Heinrich Adolph Schrader]] in 1821,<ref name=IPNI_17132-1/> with the only species (and so the [[Type (biology)|type species]]) being ''[[Nematanthus corticola]]'',<ref name=Schr21/> one of the species with flowers hanging down on long pedicels.<ref name=GS/> The name ''Nematanthus'' is from [[Ancient Greek]] ''nema'' meaning 'thread' and ''anthos'' meaning 'flower', referring to the {{cvt|8|in|cm|order=flip}} long pedicels of the type species.<ref name=GS/>

''Nematanthus'' is placed in the subfamily [[Gesnerioideae]], tribe Gesnerieae, subtribe Columneinae.<ref name=WebeMiddClarMoll20/> Within the subtribe, it forms a clade with ''[[Codonanthe]]'', ''[[Codonanthopsis]]'' and ''[[Lesia (plant)|Lesia]]'':<ref name=SmitClar13/><ref name=ChauPerr13/>

== Cultivation ==
''Nematanthus'' thrive at temperatures between {{cvt|18|and|25|C|F}}, although they stay more compact if grown at {{cvt|15|to|17|C|F}}.<ref name=Lent87/> They may lose their leaves if temperatures go above this level.<ref name=Lent87/><ref name=GRW/> ''Nematanthus gregarius'' is said to tolerate temperatures down to {{cvt|30|to|35|F|C|order=flip}}.<ref name=GardOrg/> ''Nematanthus'' do best in bright indirect light,<ref name=Lent87/> and can easily burn in direct sunlight. They prefer high humidity, and grow better under these conditions, but adapt to household humidity.<ref name=GRW/><ref name=PCT/> The tuberous roots of this plant retain water, and ''Nematanthus'' prefer the soil to remain moist, and well-drained. The goldfish plant enjoys being pot-bound, and is more likely to bloom in that state. When grown in the right conditions, ''Nematanthus'' is known to bloom year-round. To encourage new blooms, regular pruning of the plant is recommended.<ref name=GHP/> Plants can be propagated from [[Cutting (plant)|cuttings]].<ref name=Lent87/>

===Cultivars===
[[File:Nematanthus 'Tropicana' 091215.jpg|thumb|''Nematanthus'' 'Tropicana']]
[[File:Nematanthus Dibleys Gold 3zz.jpg|thumb|''Nematanthus gregarius'' 'Dibley's Gold']]
'Tropicana' originated from a cross made in the United States by W. R. Saylor. The parents were reported to be ''N. perianthomegus'' and ''N. gregarius''.<ref name=Lent87/> {{As of|2021|April}}, ''N. perianthomegus'' was treated as a synonym of ''N. hirtellus'' by Plants of the World Online,<ref name=POWO_168209-2/> although other sources say that it is a synonym of ''N. tessmannii''.<ref name=GS/> 'Tropicana' is initially upright, after which older branches trail. The leaves are {{cvt|5|by|2.5|cm|in|1}}, glossy dark green with a reddish brown margin on the under surface. The flower has a red-brown [[Sepal|calyx]], the fused [[petal]]s (perianth) being yellow with red-brown stripes and spots. 'Tropicana' produces flower buds all year round.<ref name=Lent87/>

'Rio' also originated from a cross by Saylor, in this case between ''N. gregarius'' and ''N. fissus'' (syn. ''Hypocyrta selloana''). Its leaves are slightly larger than those of 'Tropicana', {{cvt|6|by|6|cm|in|1}}, lighter green on both sides and less glossy. The flower is smaller, with a light green calyx and a striking orange-red perianth. 'Rio' makes buds all year round.<ref name=Lent87/>

'Herens' is of unknown origin. It resembles 'Tropicana', with a somewhat smaller leaf, {{cvt|4.5|by|2|cm|in|1}}, with a reddish tinge on the underside. The calyx is red-green and the perianth orange-red. It can flower abundantly all year round.<ref name=Lent87/>

'Gietvoz' is also of unknown origin. It is a compact cultivar, less sensitive to unfavorable growing conditions such as overwatering or bright light. The leaf is smaller, {{cvt|3.5|by|2|cm|in|1}}, and less tapered than that of other cultivars, and is thick, waxy and glossy. The underside of the leaf is red with a green edge and is clearly visible as the leaves are somewhat upright. The flower has an inconspicuous light green calyx and an orange-yellow perianth. Although 'Gietvoz' does not flower as readily as other cultivars, it has a good growth habit and attractive foliage.<ref name=Lent87/>

Saylor also made crosses between ''[[Codonanthe gracilis]]'' and ''Nematanthus'' hybrids, creating the hybrid genus [[× Codonatanthus|× ''Codonatanthus'']]. Two of the resulting cultivars are 'Fiesta' and 'Aurora'.<ref name=Sayl78/><ref name=Lent87/>

''Nematanthus gregarius'' 'Dibley's Gold' has variegated leaves.<ref name=GRW/>

== Toxicity ==
''Nematanthus'' is considered non-toxic and safe for pets by the [[American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals|ASPCA.]]<ref name=ASPCA/>
